missing_diagrams.diagram_kind: Grover-iterate quantum circuit with address and response wires
missing_diagrams.rationale: The item specifies preparation, one standard bit query, phase kickback, the marked-state phase oracle, and the address reflection in sequence. A circuit schematic would make the register roles and unchanged response state easier to track.
missing_diagrams.draw_or_check: Show the address register entering the query; show the response wire prepared by X then H from |0> to |->; apply U_f jointly, label the address action after kickback O_M, then apply R_s only to the address register. Mark the response as |-> throughout after the query and show no intermediate measurement. Keep preparation/reflection costs distinct from the one query.
missing_diagrams.status: candidate only; the source directly supports every wire and operation, and the text itself is legible.

missing_diagrams.diagram_kind: Unary-clock history path and one local propagation transition
missing_diagrams.rationale: The procedure defines a padded gate sequence, legal unary clock states, endpoint-specific clock patterns, and a five-local transition term. A compact diagram could connect clock advancement to application of U_l on the data register.
missing_diagrams.draw_or_check: Show |c_0>, |c_1>, …, |c_N> as a path with data states |psi_0>, U_1|psi_0>, …, U_N…U_1|psi_0>. For an interior step, label clock bits (l−1,l,l+1) with 100 ↔ 110 and indicate U_l on the data wire in the forward direction and U_l* in reverse. Separately label the stated l=1 and l=N boundary patterns; do not depict the legal clock as a single excitation.
missing_diagrams.status: candidate only; source equations support the displayed transition and endpoint conventions; no correctness claim should depend on the diagram.

missing_diagrams.diagram_kind: QSVT action on one singular-value invariant plane
missing_diagrams.rationale: The theorem reduces the circuit to a two-dimensional invariant plane for each positive singular value, then reads the upper-left entry of the ordered phase sequence as P_Phi(sigma_j). A labeled plane diagram would make this reduction and its compressed block action easier to follow.
missing_diagrams.draw_or_check: Use input basis (v_j,w_j) and output basis (u_j,w_tilde_j); label U by W_R(sigma_j)=[[sigma_j,sqrt(1−sigma_j^2)],[sqrt(1−sigma_j^2),−sigma_j]]. Show the ordered product Z(phi_0)W_R Z(phi_1)…W_R Z(phi_d)=U_Phi(sigma_j) and highlight its upper-left entry P_Phi(sigma_j), corresponding to |u_j><v_j| in odd parity or |v_j><v_j| in even parity. State that sigma=0,1 are separate endpoint cases.
missing_diagrams.status: candidate only; all plane bases, matrices, phase order, and parity outputs are stated in the source.

review_scope: Frozen Quantum Algorithms lane 02 assignment snapshots and local HTML only; no production route or live-site claims.
